Agents here (t3, Claude Code, Codex sessions) share the same memory as
whatever test or build they launch. One runaway test can use 6GB on its own,
and the machine then swaps hard or the kernel OOM killer fires.

## Why it matters

The kernel kills the biggest process, which is usually the runaway test, not
the agents. On nixed, `flutter_tester` (~6GB) was killed three times on
2026-10-18. Before `OOMPolicy=continue` was set on `t3.service`, systemd then
stopped the whole unit and every agent session in it died too. That setting
is now in `scout-modules/t3`, but the box is still thrashing the whole time
before the kill. Keep tests small and capped so it never comes to that.

## Heavy work goes to Boat first

**Prefer Boat (cloud sandboxes) for all heavy work**: test runs beyond one or
two files, suites, builds, APKs, long benchmarks. Use
`edge.research/bin/boat-run [--shell PREFIX] <worktree> -- <command>`: it syncs
the worktree, fixes the Nix socket, runs detached and returns the exit code and
the log (see the `boat` skill). Queuing heavy runs in qex on these 8GB hosts
cost 20 to 120 minutes of waiting on 2026-11-11, and Boat has no memory
problem. Briefs to subagents name `boat-run`, not a local runner.

- for one or two quick runs (a single test file, a small build), or

  hours are at or below the threshold (default 10%). Read it with `vigil advice`

  `vigil advisory set boat-budget threshold=<percent>`. If the advice says it
  is unavailable, prefer Boat and check `boat limits` yourself.

## Queue the local jobs through qex

other agents are about to start. On 2026-11-10 two
sessions' Rust and Gradle builds plus a test run caused 8 OOM kills in 25
minutes on nixed. `qex` is the shared queue: a job claims cores and memory,

# build-loop reference: scope, pilots, estimates, fast iteration (§1, §2, §4, §8–9)

Source: edge "live guides r2" (2026-11-13) and "no-spinners" (2026-11-15).

## The scope question (§1)

Ask the owner which kind of change this is:

- **Pilot**: try it on a few cases, gather data, then decide.
- **Structural fix**: change how the thing works everywhere.
- **Hardening**: strengthen the structural design before an upstream PR or project release.

**Default: pilot.** Owner: "The answer is typically launch things as pilots first, because then we're
able to gather more data and that data is able to inform implementations that are correct the first
time." Ask inline with that default and keep working (§1a). A bug fix is not a pilot; skip the
question when the kind is obvious.

## Pilot rules

- **Scored, agreed before starting (owner, 2026-11-15).** Agree the feature's scored concerns and
  bars with the owner, typically four: data safety (`durability`), correctness (`error-paths`), the
  feature goal (`legibility` for UX, `performance` for layout shift), maintainability (`architecture`).
  Record exactly those concerns at init, for example `init --pilot --bar durability=9 --bar wiring=7
  --bars-agreed "<owner quote or note>"`. Concern names come from `bars.md`.
  Without an agreement, touched concerns default to 6, except durability at 7. If the pilot writes
  stored data, changes schema or migrations, or sends notifications or other outward messages,
  pass `--touches-data`: durability
  defaults to 9 and is included automatically. `durable-state`/`migration` categories also select it.
  Init prints the default applied. Pilots never record or constrain a region's shape/stage in
  `bars.json`. Structural and later stages keep the normal shape × stage bars.
- **Review schedule.** Round 1: Sol or Opus, never the author. Round 2: Fable, including ARGUE,
  STEP-BACK, NIT-CULL and FIX-KEPT; later rounds keep the normal caps. Every named concern must
  meet its bar, and the owner must approve the pilot build. Record `review-ledger -l L owner-ok
  "<quote>"`; without it the ledger refuses CHECKPOINT and STOP-AGREED.
- **Hardening list.** Use the existing `HARDENING-STASH`, not a second list. Review briefs send
  findings outside the agreed concerns, or not needed for the current bars, there. Do not fix them
  this round. Typical items: pixel/frame tests and sweeps, stricter measurement, micro-performance,
  screen readers, translations of changing copy, maintainability tidy-ups.
- **Tests cover the pilot's own cases only.** No sweeps over every item, no catalogue-wide guards,
  until the owner decides to go structural. Size check: pilot test code stays under about twice the
  expected change. Over that, cut tests before writing more.
- **No full test runs (owner, 2026-11-15).** The pilot stage runs targeted tests and gates for what
  it touches. Full runs belong to the structural and hardening stages.
- **One red round.** The spec review (§4a) may run alongside green, not before it. Its findings go to
  the first fix round.
- **Ship iteration builds early.** An iteration build, preview or screenshot set goes to the owner as soon as the
  targeted tests pass. The pilot's scored review (§6) follows the owner's feedback.
- **Opt-in.** Put pilot behaviour behind a flag or a per-item field, so the pilot build changes only
  the pilot's cases.
- **Own branch, kept as a reference (owner, 2026-11-15).** Keep the pilot branch as a reference.
  Start the structural stage fresh from the base on a new branch, carrying over only the code,
  tests and evidence the owner endorsed. Pilot tests encode the pilot design; rebuilding avoids
  spending the structural round undoing it.
- **End with evidence** for the owner's decision: before/after shots, counts, what broke.

Structural and hardening stages use the normal bars and review schedule (§4–§6).

## Stages and what to test (§1, §3)

The work stages are pilot → structural → hardening:

- **Pilot**: a few cases, opt-in; tests cover the pilot's own cases only (above).
- **Structural**: the owner says go wide. One design check per fix; looser on edge cases.
- **Hardening**: before an upstream PR opens or goes ready, or a project release, review the
  hardening stash at normal bars. Add symptom tests, catalogue sweeps, pixel/frame tests, edge cases.

Before a structural round lands on an integration branch the owner runs: the structural review
at normal bars, Fable at round 3, no extra triage. Before an upstream PR or a project release: hardening.

**Test the design, not the symptom, until hardening.** When a fix rules a bug out by construction,
one assertion that the construction is in place is the test. Symptom tests (frame stepping, pixel
sampling, timing, sweeps over every item) are hardening work.

**30-minute flag.** An implementer that spends more than 30 minutes on one problem (the same failing
test or symptom across 3 or more runs) flags it to the orchestrator in its report and keeps working on
the rest. The orchestrator cuts it (defers it to hardening) or asks the owner. Put this rule in every
implementer brief, next to: "You may use vigil, but never orchestrator mode (`orchestrator: true` /
`--orchestrator`); that is only for the main session that talks with the user."

# Writing copy

Load `unslop` and `plain-writing` first, then apply these six rules.

1. **No eyebrow lines.** Omit the small label or kicker above a heading or
   title unless the request asks for one.
2. **Question every piece of text.** Name the question it answers and whether
   anyone is really asking it. People usually are not. Cut it if not.
3. **Keep jargon out of explainers.** One word per idea, defined once. Reuse
   that word; do not cycle synonyms.
4. **One named audience.** Know who reads it before you write, and write for
   that person.
5. **No compliance narration.** Do not explain how an action follows a rule
   or why it does not break one, unless the reader asked or the action really
   sits on the rule's boundary; then state the decision in one clause and stop.
   Never explain a distinction the reader set up or plainly knows. After a
   correction, report what changed; do not reassure in later messages. The
   test: what would the reader misread without this sentence? If nothing, cut
   it.
6. **Three passes before sending.** Reread the whole draft three times, each
   pass with one question: is every claim correct; does every sentence answer
   something the reader is asking; is any sentence about the writer rather
   than the reader's subject (self-justification, reassurance, credit, effort).
   Take the most care with that last kind: it is the easiest to miss in your
   own writing. Fix and reread after each pass.

Subagents load `unslop` and `plain-writing` only when they write copy, or when
a reviewer fixes comments (build-loop A7).

  STEP-BACK, NIT-CULL and FIX-KEPT; later rounds keep the normal caps. Every named concern must
  meet its bar, and the owner must approve the pilot build. Record `review-ledger -l L owner-ok
  "<quote>"`; without it the ledger refuses CHECKPOINT and STOP-AGREED.
- **Hardening list.** Use the existing `HARDENING-STASH`, not a second list. Review briefs send
  findings outside the agreed concerns, or not needed for the current bars, there. Do not fix them
  this round. Typical items: pixel/frame tests and sweeps, stricter measurement, micro-performance,
  screen readers, translations of changing copy, maintainability tidy-ups.
- **Tests cover the pilot's own cases only.** No sweeps over every item, no catalogue-wide guards,
  until the owner decides to go structural. Size check: pilot test code stays under about twice the
  expected change. Over that, cut tests before writing more.
- **No full test runs (owner, 2026-11-15).** The pilot stage runs targeted tests and gates for what
  it touches. Full runs belong to the structural and hardening stages.
- **One red round.** The spec review (§4a) may run alongside green, not before it. Its findings go to
  the first fix round.
- **Ship iteration builds early.** An iteration build, preview or screenshot set goes to the owner as soon as the
  targeted tests pass. The pilot's scored review (§6) follows the owner's feedback.
- **Opt-in.** Put pilot behaviour behind a flag or a per-item field, so the pilot build changes only
  the pilot's cases.

  spending the structural round undoing it.

The work stages are pilot → structural → hardening:

- **Pilot**: a few cases, opt-in; tests cover the pilot's own cases only (above).
- **Structural**: the owner says go wide. One design check per fix; looser on edge cases.
- **Hardening**: before an upstream PR opens or goes ready, or a project release, review the
  hardening stash at normal bars. Add symptom tests, catalogue sweeps, pixel/frame tests, edge cases.

Before a structural round lands on an integration branch the owner runs: the structural review
at normal bars, Fable at round 3, no extra triage. Before an upstream PR or a project release: hardening.

one assertion that the construction is in place is the test. Symptom tests (frame stepping, pixel
sampling, timing, sweeps over every item) are hardening work.

---
name: technical-excellence
description: >-
  Design and code standards for work that must stay correct: rich interfaces
  (errors, reason, invariants, parity tests), cited claims with grep-able ids,
  deep modules, a project lexicon with disciplined naming, type-level safety
  (invalid states unrepresentable, monoids, exhaustive matching), and a
  threat-model check on security. Use when designing an abstraction, writing or
  reviewing code or comments, naming things, or judging a review finding.
  Companions: test-quality (proving it), build-loop (the workflow).
---

# technical-excellence

Standards for what the code says and how it is shaped.

| Skill | Load it when |
|---|---|
| `test-quality` | Writing or reviewing the tests that prove an interface, claim or invariant here. |
| `build-loop` | The work is multi-phase, or a cross-model review will judge it. Its review step uses sections 6 and 7 below. |

First rule: **when in Rome.** Follow the repo's conventions (AGENTS.md,
existing style, lexicon) before anything below. Apply this skill where the repo
is silent.

## 1. Rich interfaces

An interface is more than signatures. Each abstraction documents:

| Part | Says |
|---|---|
| Error detail | What can fail, and how it is reported (type, code, null, exception). Callers must be able to handle each case without reading the body. |
| Reason | Why it exists. What breaks or duplicates if it is removed. |
| Invariants | What is always true before, during and after calls. |
| Mating parts | If it has a second or third counterpart (writer/reader, encoder/decoder, client/server), name them. |

**Mated parts need parity tests** proving both sides agree: round trip, plus
independent fixtures (see `test-quality`, parity and oracles). A pair that is
only tested against each other's constants proves nothing.

## 2. Claims are cited

Module-level comments and comments above code blocks contain verifiable
claims ("this is O(n)", "the device sends big-endian", "idempotent",
"commit happens before ACK"). Every such claim is anchored and sourced.

Convention (adapt the comment syntax to the language):

```
// CLAIM(ack-order): the commit completes before the ACK is sent [spec §4.2; ack_order_test]
...
// ↳ CLAIM(ack-order)
ack(token);
```

- The comment states a **verifiable** claim and its **source or proof** in
  brackets: a spec section, capture file, proof sketch, or test name.
- The code the claim governs carries `↳ CLAIM(<id>)`.
- A maintainer changing that code greps the id, finds the claim and its
  proof, and re-checks it.
- Tests that prove the claim name the id in their why (`test-quality`).
- Ids are short, unique, stable. Unprovable "claims" are opinions: label them
  as such or delete them. A comment with no source is a rumor.

## 3. Deep modules

Prefer a simple interface over a substantial implementation. Few entry
points, few parameters, no leaked internals. Smells: shallow wrappers that
forward one call; interfaces as long as the body; callers that must know
call order. Hide the complexity; do not spread it across callers.

## 4. Lexicon and naming

Keep a project lexicon (a glossary doc: term, meaning, where it lives). Name
code in correspondence with it. Add a term to the glossary when you coin one;
do not use two words for one concept.

Outside any convention:

- Clear names, **no abbreviations**.
- 1-2 primary words, plus optional small words (determiners, prepositions):
  `rowsToPrune`, `nightOfRecord`.
- Be deliberate about grammar:
  - functions and methods: verbs (`parseFrame`); predicates read as
    questions (`isFinalized`, `hasPendingWrite`);
  - values and types: nouns (`dayLabel`, `HistoryToken`);
  - qualifiers: adjectives (`pendingRows`);
  - tense shows state: `committedRows` (done), `rowsToCommit` (not yet).
- Name by how the value is used, not its type. Avoid vague names such as
  `value`, `data`, `result`, `tmp`. A function that sums two numbers returns

  proving nothing. Every test states its WHY (and CLAIM id); co-located tests;
  monoid laws, model-based state-machine properties, oracles, reviewed goldens,
  parity tests for mated interfaces; cheap manual mutation checks and periodic
  mutation tooling; explicit tautology hunting; plus the full failure-mode
  catalog with detection hints and fixes (tautology, over-mocking, asserting

# Test quality

A green run says nothing about whether a test can fail. For every test you
write or review, answer one question: **if the bug came back, would this go
red?** If you can't name the bug it catches, it's hollow.

| Skill | Load it when |
|---|---|
| `technical-excellence` | The test proves an interface, invariant or CLAIM, or a type could make the test unnecessary. Source of the CLAIM convention and mated-part (parity) rule. |
| `build-loop` | You are in a red/green run or a review round. Its red gate uses this skill; review findings about tests are judged with it. |

## 1. Every test says why

The reason a test exists is hard to recall later. Annotate each test with a
short WHY: the bug, rule, incident or claim it guards.

```
// why: a partial chunk must never be ACKed (invariant 3.1; regression of the
//      2026-09 early-ack bug). Fails if commit moves after ack.
// proves: CLAIM(ack-order)
```

- A test proving a CLAIM (see `technical-excellence`) names its id, so the
  claim's grep finds its proof.
- No why, no keep: a test whose purpose nobody can state is a deletion
  candidate.
- Expected values show their derivation (spec section, capture, arithmetic).

## 2. Placement

Co-locate tests with the code they test, unless the repo's convention says
otherwise (when in Rome). A test beside its module shows what the abstraction
is, travels with it, and is deleted with it. Cross-cutting and end-to-end
suites live apart, and say so in their why.

## 3. Techniques worth using

### Monoids and accumulators
If a type combines (`combine`, identity element), property-test the laws:

| Law | Property |
|---|---|
| Identity | `combine(x, empty) == x == combine(empty, x)` |
| Associativity | `combine(combine(a,b),c) == combine(a,combine(b,c))` |

---
name: writing-copy
description: Use when writing copy, meaning any text a person outside this session reads (docs, READMEs, UI strings, PR bodies, release notes, explainers, messages to the owner). Loads unslop and plain-writing and adds rules on eyebrow lines, why each piece of text exists, jargon, audience, compliance narration and a three-pass reread.
---

# Writing copy

Load `unslop` and `plain-writing` first, then apply these six rules.

1. **No eyebrow lines.** Omit the small label or kicker above a heading or
   title unless the request asks for one.
2. **Question every piece of text.** Name the question it answers and whether
   anyone is really asking it. People usually are not. Cut it if not.
3. **Keep jargon out of explainers.** One word per idea, defined once. Reuse
   that word; do not cycle synonyms.
4. **One named audience.** Know who reads it before you write, and write for
   that person.
5. **No compliance narration.** Do not explain how an action follows a rule
   or why it does not break one, unless the reader asked or the action really
   sits on the rule's boundary; then state the decision in one clause and stop.
   Never explain a distinction the reader set up or plainly knows. After a
   correction, report what changed; do not reassure in later messages. The
   test: what would the reader misread without this sentence? If nothing, cut
   it.
6. **Three passes before sending.** Reread the whole draft three times, each
   pass with one question: is every claim correct; does every sentence answer
   something the reader is asking; is any sentence about the writer rather
   than the reader's subject (self-justification, reassurance, credit, effort).
   Take the most care with that last kind: it is the easiest to miss in your
   own writing. Fix and reread after each pass.

Subagents load `unslop` and `plain-writing` only when they write copy, or when
a reviewer fixes comments (build-loop A7).

# Boat

Boat (boat.dev) rents full Linux VMs ("sandboxes"): x86_64 Ubuntu, user
`user`, home `/home/user`, passwordless `sudo`, Docker and common toolchains,
billed per second while running. Older docs and third-party skills call it
**Box** (`box` CLI, `box.ascii.dev`, `on.ascii.dev`): same product, stale
names. Use `boat`. Inside a sandbox, agents get Boat's own `boat` skill; this
one is for driving sandboxes from here.

## Access

- The CLI is `boat` (on `PATH`; `~/.ascii/bin/boat`) and is already signed in:
  `boat status`. Never run `boat login`, `boat onboard` or an install script;
  if it says signed out, ask the user.
- A sandbox is reachable **only through the CLI** (`exec`, `ssh`, `scp`,
  `forward`). It is not on Tailscale and has no entry in `~/.ssh/config`.
- Always pass the explicit `bx_...` id. `current` and `self` do not work from
  a non-interactive shell here.
- Which sandbox: read `<project>.research/boat.md` (id, purpose, size, what
  secrets it holds). Update it when you create, trim or retire one.

## Commands

| Need | Command |
|---|---|
| State, size, TTL | `boat info <id>` (JSON; fields under `.sandbox`), `boat list` |
| Start / stop | `boat resume <id>`, `boat stop <id>` |
| Short command | `boat exec <id> --timeout 120 -- bash -lc '<cmd>'` (default timeout 30 s) |
| Long job | `boat exec <id> --detach -- bash -lc '<cmd> > ~/job.log 2>&1'` → prints `pid` |
| Wait for it | `boat exec <id> --attach <pid>` as a background Bash command (the harness notifies you); `--status <pid>`, `--kill <pid>` |
| Files | `boat scp ./f <id>:/home/user/f`, `boat scp <id>:/home/user/f ./f` |
| Source | `git bundle create x.bundle <branch>`, `scp` it, `git clone x.bundle` inside: no Git credentials enter the sandbox |
| Plan and hours | `boat limits`, `boat usage <id>`; never quote prices from memory |

`exec` prints one JSON line (`stdout`, `stderr`, exit code). Parse it, for
example `| python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.loads(sys.stdin.readline()); print(d["stdout"])'`.

## Gotchas seen here

- **Nix socket after resume.** The first Nix call after `resume` fails with
  "Permission denied" on the daemon socket. A plain restart can leave the
  socket at mode 0644, and a `chmod 666` alone later gives "Connection refused"
  once a detached job starts. What works (one `exec`): `sudo systemctl stop
  nix-daemon.service nix-daemon.socket; sudo rm -f
  /nix/var/nix/daemon-socket/socket; sudo systemctl start nix-daemon.socket
  nix-daemon.service; sleep 3; sudo chmod 666
  /nix/var/nix/daemon-socket/socket; nix store ping`. Then run detached jobs
  under `setpriv` (below). Source
  `/nix/var/nix/profiles/default/etc/profile.d/nix-daemon.sh` in each `exec`.
- **Capabilities.** `exec` processes carry ambient capabilities that break
  FHS/bubblewrap tools. Wrap detached runs:
  `--detach -- setpriv --ambient-caps -all --inh-caps -all bash -lc '...'`.
- **Nothing survives a stop** except the disk: relaunch services after
  `resume`. The IP changes on each resume.
- **Size.** Boat counts allocated disk; a sandbox past the default limit needs
  `--type large` to resume (2× cost). Trim or `nix-store --gc` instead of
  upsizing, and ask before choosing a paid size.
- **Memory.** Sandboxes have their own RAM (the qex queue is for this host),
  but default size is ~8 GB: one Gradle or emulator job at a time.

## Rules

- **Secrets stay put.** Never copy keys, tokens or signing keystores into a
  sandbox, and never print them, unless the user said so for that sandbox.
  `holdsCreatorLogins` in `info` shows whether account logins are on it; a
  sandbox made with `--no-env` has none.
- **Costs.** Stop a sandbox when the work is done. Create one only when the
  task needs it; never delete one unless the user asks. Sandboxes owned by
  another project or session are theirs: check (`boat exec <id> -- ps`) before
  touching one, and never stop one that is busy.

## Spend: cheap by default, fast under a deadline

Plan hours are finite (`boat limits`: `planIncluded.vmHoursRemaining`), a
`large` sandbox bills 2x, and a keepalive bills while nothing runs. Pick the
mode from the situation and say which one you are in.

| | Cheap (default) | Time crunch (owner deadline) |
|---|---|---|
| When | No deadline given | The owner asked for a result by a time |
| Size | `default` for test iterations; `large` only for full suites, APK builds and jobs that need its RAM | `large` throughout |
| Idle | Sandbox stops itself ~15 min after the last job (`boat-run` and `boat-sync-test` set the idle TTL); stop it explicitly at the end of a batch | Keep it up for the window; still stop it when the deadline work is delivered |
| Runs | Targeted files; batch checks into one run; full suite only at a gate (before pushing a shared branch) | Same targeting; run independent jobs in parallel; start a warm build early |
| Never | Leave a sandbox up overnight, or a 2-hour keepalive for one quick run | Run past the deadline work at `large` "while you are there" |

Check the spend once a session (`boat limits`, `boat usage <id>`) and say it
when the remaining hours will not reach the plan's period end at the current
rate. Shrinking (`boat resume <id> --type default`) needs the data to fit:
trim old run directories and `nix-store --gc` first.
- **Docs.** `https://docs.boat.dev/llms.txt` lists every page; fetch any page
  as `.md`. `boat <command> --help` is authoritative for flags.

# Running on RAM-constrained hosts (sonic and nixed)

**Both sonic and nixed need this.** Neither is a big machine:

| Host | RAM | Swap |
|------|-----|------|
| sonic (CF-19, x86_64) | 8GB | zram + disk swap partition |
| nixed (M1, aarch64) | ~7.4GB | zram (3.7GB) + 8GB swapfile |

void has plenty of memory; this skill is not for it.

Agents here (t3, Claude Code, Codex sessions) share the same memory as
whatever test or build they launch. One runaway test can use 6GB on its own,
and the machine then swaps hard or the kernel OOM killer fires.

## Why it matters

The kernel kills the biggest process, which is usually the runaway test, not
the agents. On nixed, `flutter_tester` (~6GB) was killed three times on
2026-10-18. Before `OOMPolicy=continue` was set on `t3.service`, systemd then
stopped the whole unit and every agent session in it died too. That setting
is now in `scout-modules/t3`, but the box is still thrashing the whole time
before the kill. Keep tests small and capped so it never comes to that.

## Heavy work goes to Boat first

**Prefer Boat (cloud sandboxes) for all heavy work**: test runs beyond one or
two files, suites, builds, APKs, long benchmarks. Use
`edge.research/bin/boat-run [--shell PREFIX] <worktree> -- <command>`: it syncs
the worktree, fixes the Nix socket, runs detached and returns the exit code and
the log (see the `boat` skill). Queuing heavy runs in qex on these 8GB hosts
cost 20 to 120 minutes of waiting on 2026-11-11, and Boat has no memory
problem. Briefs to subagents name `boat-run`, not a local runner.
Boat spends plan hours: use the boat skill's "Spend" table (cheap by default: `default`
size for test iterations, sandbox stops itself between batches; `large` and keep-up only under an
owner deadline).

Use qex on this host only:

- for one or two quick runs (a single test file, a small build), or
- when the `boat-budget` vigil advisory says Boat is low: Boat's remaining
  hours are at or below the threshold (default 10%). Read it with `vigil advice`
  (it is also in every `keepalive` result's `advice`). The threshold is
  `vigil advisory set boat-budget threshold=<percent>`. If the advice says it
  is unavailable, prefer Boat and check `boat limits` yourself.

## Queue the local jobs through qex

Whatever stays local (see above) goes through the queue. Agents can't see what
other agents are about to start. On 2026-11-10 two
sessions' Rust and Gradle builds plus a test run caused 8 OOM kills in 25
minutes on nixed. `qex` is the shared queue: a job claims cores and memory,
and qex starts it only when the claim fits the budget (75% of the machine,
less what other users hold). Load the `qex` skill, or run `qex help agents`.

```sh
qex list                 # who holds what now, and why anything waits
qex info                 # the budget and the load
qex submit --wait --cpu 2 --mem 3GB --id-file /tmp/<you>.id -- <command>
```

- Run `qex submit --wait` as a background command of your harness; the harness
  reports the end. Reattach with `qex status $(cat <id-file>) --wait`. No
  pgrep or sleep loops.
- Claim what the job really uses. Starting points on these hosts: `flutter
  test` 2GB, Gradle/APK build 3GB, `cargo build -j2` 2GB, `nix build` 2GB.
  qex learns from each run of the same command.
- A claim is a promise, not a limit. Put the scope cap below inside the job:
  `qex submit --wait --mem 3GB -- systemd-run --user --scope -q -p MemoryMax=4G -- <command>`.
- Never skip the queue because it is slow. A waiting job is cheaper than an
  OOM kill of someone else's work.
- But a job that has waited for memory for more than ~20 minutes should move
  to Boat instead (cancel it with `qex cancel <id>`). A queued job is still
  in flight: keep the keepalive tick live while it waits.

# build-loop reference: scope, pilots, estimates, fast iteration (§1, §2, §4, §8–9)

Source: edge "live guides r2" (2026-11-13) and "no-spinners" (2026-11-15).

## The scope question (§1)

Ask the owner which kind of change this is:

- **Pilot**: try it on a few cases, gather data, then decide.
- **Structural fix**: change how the thing works everywhere.
- **Hardening**: strengthen the structural design before an upstream PR or project release.

**Default: pilot.** Owner: "The answer is typically launch things as pilots first, because then we're
able to gather more data and that data is able to inform implementations that are correct the first
time." Ask inline with that default and keep working (§1a). A bug fix is not a pilot; skip the
question when the kind is obvious.

## Pilot rules

- **Scored, agreed before starting (owner, 2026-11-15).** Agree the feature's scored concerns and
  bars with the owner, typically four: data safety (`durability`), correctness (`error-paths`), the
  feature goal (`legibility` for UX, `performance` for layout shift), maintainability (`architecture`).
  Record exactly those concerns at init, for example `init --pilot --bar durability=9 --bar wiring=7
  --bars-agreed "<owner quote or note>"`. Concern names come from `bars.md`.
  Without an agreement, touched concerns default to 6, except durability at 7. If the pilot writes
  stored data, changes schema or migrations, or sends notifications or other outward messages,
  pass `--touches-data`: durability
  defaults to 9 and is included automatically. `durable-state`/`migration` categories also select it.
  Init prints the default applied. Pilots never record or constrain a region's shape/stage in
  `bars.json`. Structural and later stages keep the normal shape × stage bars.
- **Review schedule.** Round 1: Sol or Opus, never the author. Round 2: Fable, including ARGUE,
  STEP-BACK, NIT-CULL and FIX-KEPT; later rounds keep the normal caps. Every named concern must
  meet its bar, and the owner must approve the pilot build. Record `review-ledger -l L owner-ok
  "<quote>"`; without it the ledger refuses CHECKPOINT and STOP-AGREED.
- **Hardening list.** Use the existing `HARDENING-STASH`, not a second list. Review briefs send
  findings outside the agreed concerns, or not needed for the current bars, there. Do not fix them
  this round. Typical items: pixel/frame tests and sweeps, stricter measurement, micro-performance,
  screen readers, translations of changing copy, maintainability tidy-ups.
- **Tests cover the pilot's own cases only.** No sweeps over every item, no catalogue-wide guards,
  until the owner decides to go structural. Size check: pilot test code stays under about twice the
  expected change. Over that, cut tests before writing more.
- **No full test runs (owner, 2026-11-15).** The pilot stage runs targeted tests and gates for what
  it touches. Full runs belong to the structural and hardening stages.
- **One red round.** The spec review (§4a) may run alongside green, not before it. Its findings go to
  the first fix round.
- **Ship iteration builds early.** An iteration build, preview or screenshot set goes to the owner as soon as the
  targeted tests pass. The pilot's scored review (§6) follows the owner's feedback.
- **Opt-in.** Put pilot behaviour behind a flag or a per-item field, so the pilot build changes only
  the pilot's cases.
- **Own branch, kept as a reference (owner, 2026-11-15).** Keep the pilot branch as a reference.
  Start the structural stage fresh from the base on a new branch, carrying over only the code,
  tests and evidence the owner endorsed. Pilot tests encode the pilot design; rebuilding avoids
  spending the structural round undoing it.
- **End with evidence** for the owner's decision: before/after shots, counts, what broke.

Structural and hardening stages use the normal bars and review schedule (§4–§6).

## Stages and what to test (§1, §3)

The work stages are pilot → structural → hardening:

- **Pilot**: a few cases, opt-in; tests cover the pilot's own cases only (above).
- **Structural**: the owner says go wide. One design check per fix; looser on edge cases.
- **Hardening**: before an upstream PR opens or goes ready, or a project release, review the
  hardening stash at normal bars. Add symptom tests, catalogue sweeps, pixel/frame tests, edge cases.

Before a structural round lands on an integration branch the owner runs: the structural review
at normal bars, Fable at round 3, no extra triage. Before an upstream PR or a project release: hardening.

**Test the design, not the symptom, until hardening.** When a fix rules a bug out by construction,
one assertion that the construction is in place is the test. Symptom tests (frame stepping, pixel
sampling, timing, sweeps over every item) are hardening work.

**30-minute flag.** An implementer that spends more than 30 minutes on one problem (the same failing
test or symptom across 3 or more runs) flags it to the orchestrator in its report and keeps working on
the rest. The orchestrator cuts it (defers it to hardening) or asks the owner. Put this rule in every
implementer brief, next to: "You may use vigil, but never orchestrator mode (`orchestrator: true` /
`--orchestrator`); that is only for the main session that talks with the user."

# technical-excellence

Standards for what the code says and how it is shaped.

| Skill | Load it when |
|---|---|
| `test-quality` | Writing or reviewing the tests that prove an interface, claim or invariant here. |
| `build-loop` | The work is multi-phase, or a cross-model review will judge it. Its review step uses sections 6 and 7 below. |

First rule: **when in Rome.** Follow the repo's conventions (AGENTS.md,
existing style, lexicon) before anything below. Apply this skill where the repo
is silent.

## 1. Rich interfaces

An interface is more than signatures. Each abstraction documents:

| Part | Says |
|---|---|
| Error detail | What can fail, and how it is reported (type, code, null, exception). Callers must be able to handle each case without reading the body. |
| Reason | Why it exists. What breaks or duplicates if it is removed. |
| Invariants | What is always true before, during and after calls. |
| Mating parts | If it has a second or third counterpart (writer/reader, encoder/decoder, client/server), name them. |

**Mated parts need parity tests** proving both sides agree: round trip, plus
independent fixtures (see `test-quality`, parity and oracles). A pair that is
only tested against each other's constants proves nothing.

## 2. Claims are cited

Module-level comments and comments above code blocks contain verifiable
claims ("this is O(n)", "the device sends big-endian", "idempotent",
"commit happens before ACK"). Every such claim is anchored and sourced.

Convention (adapt the comment syntax to the language):

```
// CLAIM(ack-order): the commit completes before the ACK is sent [spec §4.2; ack_order_test]
...
// ↳ CLAIM(ack-order)
ack(token);
```

- The comment states a **verifiable** claim and its **source or proof** in
  brackets: a spec section, capture file, proof sketch, or test name.
- The code the claim governs carries `↳ CLAIM(<id>)`.
- A maintainer changing that code greps the id, finds the claim and its
  proof, and re-checks it.
- Tests that prove the claim name the id in their why (`test-quality`).
- Ids are short, unique, stable. Unprovable "claims" are opinions: label them
  as such or delete them. A comment with no source is a rumor.

## 3. Deep modules

Prefer a simple interface over a substantial implementation. Few entry
points, few parameters, no leaked internals. Smells: shallow wrappers that
forward one call; interfaces as long as the body; callers that must know
call order. Hide the complexity; do not spread it across callers.

## 4. Lexicon and naming

Keep a project lexicon (a glossary doc: term, meaning, where it lives). Name
code in correspondence with it. Add a term to the glossary when you coin one;
do not use two words for one concept.

Outside any convention:

- Clear names, **no abbreviations**.
- 1-2 primary words, plus optional small words (determiners, prepositions):
  `rowsToPrune`, `nightOfRecord`.
- Be deliberate about grammar:
  - functions and methods: verbs (`parseFrame`); predicates read as
    questions (`isFinalized`, `hasPendingWrite`);
  - values and types: nouns (`dayLabel`, `HistoryToken`);
  - qualifiers: adjectives (`pendingRows`);
  - tense shows state: `committedRows` (done), `rowsToCommit` (not yet).
- Name by how the value is used, not its type. Avoid vague names such as
  `value`, `data`, `result`, `tmp`. A function that sums two numbers returns

# Test quality

A green run says nothing about whether a test can fail. For every test you
write or review, answer one question: **if the bug came back, would this go
red?** If you can't name the bug it catches, it's hollow.

| Skill | Load it when |
|---|---|
| `technical-excellence` | The test proves an interface, invariant or CLAIM, or a type could make the test unnecessary. Source of the CLAIM convention and mated-part (parity) rule. |
| `build-loop` | You are in a red/green run or a review round. Its red gate uses this skill; review findings about tests are judged with it. |

## 1. Every test says why

The reason a test exists is hard to recall later. Annotate each test with a
short WHY: the bug, rule, incident or claim it guards.

```
// why: a partial chunk must never be ACKed (invariant 3.1; regression of the
//      2026-09 early-ack bug). Fails if commit moves after ack.
// proves: CLAIM(ack-order)
```

- A test proving a CLAIM (see `technical-excellence`) names its id, so the
  claim's grep finds its proof.
- No why, no keep: a test whose purpose nobody can state is a deletion
  candidate.
- Expected values show their derivation (spec section, capture, arithmetic).

## 2. Placement

Co-locate tests with the code they test, unless the repo's convention says
otherwise (when in Rome). A test beside its module shows what the abstraction
is, travels with it, and is deleted with it. Cross-cutting and end-to-end
suites live apart, and say so in their why.

## 3. Techniques worth using

### Monoids and accumulators
If a type combines (`combine`, identity element), property-test the laws:

| Law | Property |
|---|---|
| Identity | `combine(x, empty) == x == combine(empty, x)` |
| Associativity | `combine(combine(a,b),c) == combine(a,combine(b,c))` |
# build-loop reference: roles, defaults, budget switching (§1a, §2)

The agent cap and the role table stay in SKILL.md §2. This file holds the rest.

## 1a. Owner contact and decisions

- When the workq hook asks, file the owner's requests.
- **Asking.** Assume the user is away. Ask inline with a proposed default and
  keep working. AskUserQuestion only on request: it blocks.
- **Never block on a decision.** Pick the safe default (reversible, least
  harm, closest to the spec), apply it, and log it in a "Defaults taken" list
  (id, choice, reason). Raise each at the next check-in; if it touches reviewed
  code, ask the reviewer to judge it.
- **Genuinely blocked.** Do other planned work, or stay in cache (§10).

## 2. Role rules

- **B1 Alternate.** Outside low budget, implementers alternate by fix round:
  if Sonnet wrote the first build, Sol writes the round-1 fixes and Sonnet the
  round-2 fixes. Green may also alternate from red. Pass `--author` to the ledger.
- **B2 Poor scope.** Ask for detail first. Occasionally an Opus agent on high
  effort implements instead of Sonnet; say why.
- **B3 Fable.** A T3 delegate (`orchestrator_capabilities` lists the version;
  the Agent tool's `fable` alias returns 404 here), effort high. Never swap
  versions silently; tell the owner.
- **R2 Authors.** A reviewer never reviews code it wrote.
- **B5 Back to default.** On a usage reset, on `claude-budget` or
  `codex-budget` advice that budget is fine, or on `credit_state_changed` with
  `on_credits` false, return to the default roles at the next phase boundary,
  not mid-run (`references/budget.md`).
- **Copy (C3).** Subagents do not load `unslop` or `plain-writing` unless they
  write copy; briefs to implementers say so.

**Switch by budget.** Claude usage low: Sol implements, Opus reviews and
verifies. Sol low or at its limit: Sonnet implements, Opus reviews or waits
for Sol (§8). Never quietly substitute a model for a role the user pinned.
State who holds which role at the start of each phase.

**Batching.** Both budgets low and Sol available now and then: red for the
whole scope, then one big green run per batch. Else 1-2 phases per run.

## Set the round focus

Store a JSON object containing arrays of strings:

```json
{
  "most_important": ["Revoking a share prevents subsequent content reads."],
  "invariants": ["Cached content must not bypass revocation."],
  "priority_concerns": ["security", "concurrency"],
  "lower_priority": ["Copy polish can wait."],

}
```

The first, second and fifth arrays must be nonempty. State uncertainty honestly
when proof is missing. Priorities weight attention; they cannot waive a real
contract, security or data-loss defect. `context` updates later briefs; each

import java.security.MessageDigest
import java.security.SecureRandom
import javax.inject.Inject
import javax.inject.Singleton

/** Local opt-in credential owner. UI may copy/rotate/revoke it; no credential enters logs or tracing. */
@Singleton
class ScheduleAutomationCredentials @Inject constructor(private val preferences: SharedPreferences) : AutomationCredentials {
    override fun isEnabled(): Boolean = preferences.getBoolean(ENABLED, false)
    override fun matches(presented: String?): Boolean {
        val saved = credential() ?: return false
        if (presented?.length != 64) return false
        return MessageDigest.isEqual(saved.toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8), presented.toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8))
    }
    fun credential(): String? = preferences.getString(CREDENTIAL, null)
    fun rotate(): String {
        val bytes = ByteArray(32).also { SecureRandom().nextBytes(it) }
        val credential = bytes.joinToString("") { "%02x".format(it.toInt() and 255) }
        check(preferences.edit().putString(CREDENTIAL, credential).commit())
        return credential
    }
    fun setEnabled(enabled: Boolean) {
        require(!enabled || credential() != null) { "Create an automation credential before enabling" }
        check(preferences.edit().putBoolean(ENABLED, enabled).commit())
    }
    fun revoke() { check(preferences.edit().putBoolean(ENABLED, false).remove(CREDENTIAL).commit()) }
    companion object {
        private const val ENABLED = "notification_automation_enabled_v1"
        private const val CREDENTIAL = "notification_automation_credential_v1"
    }
}

import android.content.SharedPreferences
import ly.com.tahaben.notification_filter_domain.schedule.AutomationCredentials
import java.security.MessageDigest
import java.security.SecureRandom
import javax.inject.Inject
import javax.inject.Singleton

/** Local opt-in credential owner. UI may copy/rotate/revoke it; no credential enters logs or tracing. */
@Singleton
class ScheduleAutomationCredentials @Inject constructor(private val preferences: SharedPreferences) : AutomationCredentials {
    override fun isEnabled(): Boolean = preferences.getBoolean(ENABLED, false)
    override fun matches(presented: String?): Boolean {
        val saved = credential() ?: return false
        if (presented?.length != 64) return false
        return MessageDigest.isEqual(saved.toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8), presented.toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8))
    }
    fun credential(): String? = preferences.getString(CREDENTIAL, null)
    fun rotate(): String {
        val bytes = ByteArray(32).also { SecureRandom().nextBytes(it) }
        val credential = bytes.joinToString("") { "%02x".format(it.toInt() and 255) }
        check(preferences.edit().putString(CREDENTIAL, credential).commit())
        return credential
    }
    fun setEnabled(enabled: Boolean) {
        require(!enabled || credential() != null) { "Create an automation credential before enabling" }
        check(preferences.edit().putBoolean(ENABLED, enabled).commit())
    }
    fun revoke() { check(preferences.edit().putBoolean(ENABLED, false).remove(CREDENTIAL).commit()) }
    companion object {
        private const val ENABLED = "notification_automation_enabled_v1"
        private const val CREDENTIAL = "notification_automation_credential_v1"
    }
}

@AndroidEntryPoint
class NotificationDeliveryReceiver : BroadcastReceiver() {

    @Inject
    lateinit var deliveryEngine: NotificationDeliveryEngine

    override fun onReceive(context: Context, intent: Intent?) {
        if (intent?.action != NotificationDeliveryScheduler.ACTION_DELIVER_PENDING &&
            intent?.action != Intent.ACTION_BOOT_COMPLETED
        ) {
            return
        }

        val pendingResult = goAsync()
        CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + Dispatchers.IO).launch {
            try {
                deliveryEngine.maintainDeliverySchedule(context)
            } finally {
                pendingResult.finish()
            }
        }
    }
}

            intent?.action != Intent.ACTION_BOOT_COMPLETED
        ) {
            return
        }

        val pendingResult = goAsync()
        CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + Dispatchers.IO).launch {
            try {
                deliveryEngine.maintainDeliverySchedule(context)
            } finally {
                pendingResult.finish()
            }
        }
    }

import java.security.MessageDigest

import javax.inject.Inject

/** Local opt-in credential owner. UI may copy/rotate/revoke it; no credential enters logs or tracing. */
@Singleton
class ScheduleAutomationCredentials @Inject constructor(private val preferences: SharedPreferences) : AutomationCredentials {
    override fun isEnabled(): Boolean = preferences.getBoolean(ENABLED, false)
    override fun matches(presented: String?): Boolean {
        val saved = credential() ?: return false
        if (presented?.length != 64) return false
        return MessageDigest.isEqual(saved.toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8), presented.toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8))
    }
    fun credential(): String? = preferences.getString(CREDENTIAL, null)
    fun rotate(): String {
        val bytes = ByteArray(32).also { SecureRandom().nextBytes(it) }
        val credential = bytes.joinToString("") { "%02x".format(it.toInt() and 255) }
        check(preferences.edit().putString(CREDENTIAL, credential).commit())
        return credential
    }
    fun setEnabled(enabled: Boolean) {
        require(!enabled || credential() != null) { "Create an automation credential before enabling" }
        check(preferences.edit().putBoolean(ENABLED, enabled).commit())
    }
    fun revoke() { check(preferences.edit().putBoolean(ENABLED, false).remove(CREDENTIAL).commit()) }
    companion object {
        private const val ENABLED = "notification_automation_enabled_v1"
        private const val CREDENTIAL = "notification_automation_credential_v1"
    }
}

        return DefaultPreferences(sharedPreferences, dataStore)

@AndroidEntryPoint
class NotificationDeliveryReceiver : BroadcastReceiver() {

    @Inject
    lateinit var deliveryEngine: NotificationDeliveryEngine

    override fun onReceive(context: Context, intent: Intent?) {
        if (intent?.action != NotificationDeliveryScheduler.ACTION_DELIVER_PENDING &&
            intent?.action != Intent.ACTION_BOOT_COMPLETED
        ) {
            return
        }

        val pendingResult = goAsync()
        CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + Dispatchers.IO).launch {
            try {
                deliveryEngine.maintainDeliverySchedule(context)
            } finally {
                pendingResult.finish()
            }
        }
    }
}

import android.content.Context
import ly.com.tahaben.notification_filter_domain.delivery.NotificationDeliveryCoordinator
import ly.com.tahaben.notification_filter_domain.preferences.Preferences
import javax.inject.Inject
import javax.inject.Singleton

/** Alarm/listener adapter. All policy and accounting belongs to the injected coordinator. */
@Singleton
class NotificationDeliveryEngine @Inject constructor(
    private val preferences: Preferences,
    private val coordinator: NotificationDeliveryCoordinator,
    private val deliveryScheduler: NotificationDeliveryScheduler,
) {
    suspend fun maintainDeliverySchedule(context: Context) {
        if (!preferences.isServiceEnabled()) return
        deliverPendingNotifications(context)
        deliveryScheduler.scheduleNextBoundaryDelivery(context)
    }
    suspend fun deliverPendingNotifications(context: Context) {
        if (preferences.isServiceEnabled()) coordinator.onBatchTick()
    }
}

@Composable
fun NotificationFilterSettingsScreen(
    onNavigateUp: () -> Unit,
    viewModel: NotificationSettingsViewModel = hiltViewModel(),
    shouldShowRational: (String) -> Boolean,
    snackbarHostState: SnackbarHostState,
    isDarkMode: Boolean
) {
    val spacing = LocalSpacing.current
    val context = LocalContext.current
    val state = viewModel._state.collectAsStateWithLifecycle().value
    val dialogQueue = state.visiblePermissionDialogQueue
    val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
    var checkKey by remember {
        mutableStateOf(false)
    }

    val postNotificationPermissionResultLauncher = rememberLauncherForActivityResult(
        contract = ActivityResultContracts.RequestPermission(),
        onResult = { isGranted ->
            if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.TIRAMISU) {
                viewModel.onPermissionResult(
                    permission = Manifest.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS,
                    isGranted = isGranted
                )
            }
        }
    )

    val postNotificationPermissionSilentCheck = rememberLauncherForActivityResult(
        contract = ActivityResultContracts.RequestPermission(),
        onResult = { isGranted ->
            if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.TIRAMISU && !isGranted) {
                viewModel.onEvent(NotificationSettingsEvent.DeclinedPermission(Manifest.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS))
            }
            checkKey = !checkKey
        }
    )

    LaunchedEffect(key1 = true) {
        viewModel.event.collect { event ->
            when (event) {
                is UiEventNotificationSettings.NotifyMeEnabled -> {
                    if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.TIRAMISU) {
                        viewModel.checkExactAlarmsPermissionGranted()
                        postNotificationPermissionResultLauncher.launch(
                            Manifest.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS
                        )
                    }
                }

                is UiEventNotificationSettings.PerformSilentChecks -> {
                    if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.TIRAMISU && state.isNotifyMeEnabled) {
                        postNotificationPermissionSilentCheck.launch(Manifest.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS)
                        viewModel.exactAlarmsSilentCheck()
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    LaunchedEffect(key1 = checkKey) {
        if (state.declinedPermissions.isNotEmpty()) {
            if (dialogQueue.isEmpty()) {
                scope.launch {
                    val result = snackbarHostState.showSnackbar(
                        context.getString(R.string.notify_me_permissions_needed_not_granted),
                        actionLabel = context.getString(
                            R.string.grant_access
                        ),
                        duration = SnackbarDuration.Indefinite
                    )
                    when (result) {
                        SnackbarResult.ActionPerformed -> {
                            Timber.d("action performed: declined permissions: ${state.declinedPermissions.toList()} size: ${state.declinedPermissions.size}")
                            dialogQueue.addAll(state.declinedPermissions.toList())
                            state.declinedPermissions.clear()
                        }

                        else -> Unit
                    }
                }
            }
        } else {
            snackbarHostState.currentSnackbarData?.dismiss()
        }
    }
    val msgStyle = ShowcaseMsg("", msgBackground = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.background, roundedCorner = 15.dp, textStyle = TextStyle(color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onBackground))
    val annotatedString = getAnnotatedStringResource( R.string.notification_filter_settings_greeting)

    ShowcaseLayout(
        isDarkLayout = isDarkMode,
        greeting = msgStyle.copy(annotatedString),
        isShowcasing = state.isShowcaseOn,
        onFinish = {
            viewModel.onEvent(NotificationSettingsEvent.OnShouldShowcase(false))
        }) {
        val filterSwitchMsg = msgStyle.copy(getAnnotatedStringResource(id = R.string.notification_filter_settings_showcase_msg1), arrow = Arrow(head = Head.TRIANGLE, color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.background))
        val notifyMeMsg1 = msgStyle.copy(getAnnotatedStringResource(id = R.string.notification_filter_settings_showcase_msg5))
        val notifyMeMsg2 = msgStyle.copy(getAnnotatedStringResource(id = R.string.notification_filter_settings_showcase_msg6), arrow = Arrow(targetFrom = Side.Top, head = Head.TRIANGLE, color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.background))
        Column(
            Modifier
                .fillMaxSize()
        ) {
            TopAppBar(
                title = {
                    Text(text = stringResource(id = R.string.notifications_filter_settings))
                },
                colors = TopAppBarDefaults.topAppBarColors(containerColor = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.background),
                navigationIcon = {
                    IconButton(onClick = onNavigateUp) {
                        Icon(
                            modifier = Modifier.mirror(),

                    }
                }
            )
            Column(
                modifier = Modifier
                    .padding(horizontal = spacing.spaceMedium)
            ) {
                Row(
                    modifier = Modifier
                        .fillMaxWidth()
                        .showcase(1, filterSwitchMsg)
                        .padding(vertical = spacing.spaceMedium)
                        .selectable(
                            selected = state.isServiceEnabled,
                            onClick = {
                                viewModel.setServiceStats(!state.isServiceEnabled)
                            },
                            role = Role.Switch
                        ),
                    horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.SpaceBetween,
                    verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically,
                    ) {
                    Text(text = stringResource(R.string.notifications_filter))
                    Switch(
                        checked = state.isServiceEnabled,

                            viewModel.setServiceStats(checked)
                        }
                    )
                }
                Divider()
                Row(
                    modifier = Modifier
                        .fillMaxWidth()
                        .showcase(2, notifyMeMsg1)
                        .showcase(3, notifyMeMsg2)
                        .padding(vertical = spacing.spaceMedium)
                        .selectable(
                            selected = state.isNotifyMeEnabled,
                            onClick = {
                                if (state.isNotifyMeEnabled) {
                                    viewModel.onEvent(NotificationSettingsEvent.CancelNotifyMe)
                                } else {
                                    viewModel.onEvent(NotificationSettingsEvent.ShowNotifyMeTimePicker)
                                }
                            },
                            role = Role.Switch
                        ),
                    horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.SpaceBetween,
                    verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically,
                ) {
                    Column {
                        Text(text = stringResource(R.string.notify_me))
                        Text(
                            text = stringResource(R.string.notify_me_description),
                            textAlign = TextAlign.Start
                        )
                    }
                    Switch(
                        checked = state.isNotifyMeEnabled,
                        onCheckedChange = { checked ->
                            if (!checked) {
                                viewModel.setNotifyMeTime(-1, -1)
                            } else {
                                viewModel.onEvent(NotificationSettingsEvent.ShowNotifyMeTimePicker)
                            }
                        }
                    )
                }
                Divider()
                Row(
                    modifier = Modifier
                        .fillMaxWidth()
                        .padding(vertical = spacing.spaceMedium)
                        .selectable(
                            selected = state.isDeliveryTestingMode,
                            onClick = {
                                viewModel.onEvent(
                                    NotificationSettingsEvent.OnSetDeliveryTestingMode(!state.isDeliveryTestingMode)
                                )
                            },
                            role = Role.Switch
                        ),
                    horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.SpaceBetween,
                    verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically,
                ) {
                    Column(modifier = Modifier.weight(1f)) {
                        Text(text = "Delivery testing mode")
                        Text(
                            text = "Replace hourly delivery boundaries with 3-minute boundaries for faster testing.",
                            style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodySmall,
                            color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant,
                        )
                    }
                    Switch(
                        checked = state.isDeliveryTestingMode,
                        onCheckedChange = { enabled ->
                            viewModel.onEvent(NotificationSettingsEvent.OnSetDeliveryTestingMode(enabled))
                        }
                    )
                }
                TextButton(

                }
                val timePickerState = rememberTimePickerState()
                if (state.isTimePickerVisible) {
                    Dialog(onDismissRequest = {

                    }) {

fun NotificationFilterSettingsScreen(
    onNavigateUp: () -> Unit,
    viewModel: NotificationSettingsViewModel = hiltViewModel(),
    shouldShowRational: (String) -> Boolean,
    snackbarHostState: SnackbarHostState,
    isDarkMode: Boolean
) {
    val spacing = LocalSpacing.current
    val context = LocalContext.current
    val state = viewModel._state.collectAsStateWithLifecycle().value
    val dialogQueue = state.visiblePermissionDialogQueue
    val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
    var checkKey by remember {
        mutableStateOf(false)
    }

    val postNotificationPermissionResultLauncher = rememberLauncherForActivityResult(
        contract = ActivityResultContracts.RequestPermission(),
        onResult = { isGranted ->
            if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.TIRAMISU) {
                viewModel.onPermissionResult(
                    permission = Manifest.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS,
                    isGranted = isGranted
                )
            }
        }
    )

    val postNotificationPermissionSilentCheck = rememberLauncherForActivityResult(
        contract = ActivityResultContracts.RequestPermission(),
        onResult = { isGranted ->
            if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.TIRAMISU && !isGranted) {
                viewModel.onEvent(NotificationSettingsEvent.DeclinedPermission(Manifest.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS))
            }
            checkKey = !checkKey
        }
    )

    LaunchedEffect(key1 = true) {
        viewModel.event.collect { event ->
            when (event) {
                is UiEventNotificationSettings.NotifyMeEnabled -> {
                    if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.TIRAMISU) {
                        viewModel.checkExactAlarmsPermissionGranted()
                        postNotificationPermissionResultLauncher.launch(
                            Manifest.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS
                        )
                    }
                }

                is UiEventNotificationSettings.PerformSilentChecks -> {
                    if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.TIRAMISU && state.isNotifyMeEnabled) {
                        postNotificationPermissionSilentCheck.launch(Manifest.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS)
                        viewModel.exactAlarmsSilentCheck()
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    LaunchedEffect(key1 = checkKey) {
        if (state.declinedPermissions.isNotEmpty()) {
            if (dialogQueue.isEmpty()) {
                scope.launch {
                    val result = snackbarHostState.showSnackbar(
                        context.getString(R.string.notify_me_permissions_needed_not_granted),
                        actionLabel = context.getString(
                            R.string.grant_access
                        ),
                        duration = SnackbarDuration.Indefinite
                    )
                    when (result) {
                        SnackbarResult.ActionPerformed -> {
                            Timber.d("action performed: declined permissions: ${state.declinedPermissions.toList()} size: ${state.declinedPermissions.size}")
                            dialogQueue.addAll(state.declinedPermissions.toList())
                            state.declinedPermissions.clear()
                        }

                        else -> Unit
                    }
                }
            }
        } else {
            snackbarHostState.currentSnackbarData?.dismiss()
        }
    }
    val msgStyle = ShowcaseMsg("", msgBackground = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.background, roundedCorner = 15.dp, textStyle = TextStyle(color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onBackground))
    val annotatedString = getAnnotatedStringResource( R.string.notification_filter_settings_greeting)

    ShowcaseLayout(
        isDarkLayout = isDarkMode,
        greeting = msgStyle.copy(annotatedString),
        isShowcasing = state.isShowcaseOn,
        onFinish = {
            viewModel.onEvent(NotificationSettingsEvent.OnShouldShowcase(false))
        }) {
        val filterSwitchMsg = msgStyle.copy(getAnnotatedStringResource(id = R.string.notification_filter_settings_showcase_msg1), arrow = Arrow(head = Head.TRIANGLE, color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.background))
        val notifyMeMsg1 = msgStyle.copy(getAnnotatedStringResource(id = R.string.notification_filter_settings_showcase_msg5))
        val notifyMeMsg2 = msgStyle.copy(getAnnotatedStringResource(id = R.string.notification_filter_settings_showcase_msg6), arrow = Arrow(targetFrom = Side.Top, head = Head.TRIANGLE, color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.background))
        Column(
            Modifier
                .fillMaxSize()
        ) {
            TopAppBar(
                title = {
                    Text(text = stringResource(id = R.string.notifications_filter_settings))
                },
                colors = TopAppBarDefaults.topAppBarColors(containerColor = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.background),
                navigationIcon = {
                    IconButton(onClick = onNavigateUp) {
                        Icon(
                            modifier = Modifier.mirror(),
                            imageVector = Icons.Filled.ArrowBack,
                            contentDescription = stringResource(id = R.string.back)
                        )
                    }
                }
            )
            Column(
                modifier = Modifier
                    .padding(horizontal = spacing.spaceMedium)
            ) {
                Row(
                    modifier = Modifier
                        .fillMaxWidth()
                        .showcase(1, filterSwitchMsg)
                        .padding(vertical = spacing.spaceMedium)
                        .selectable(
                            selected = state.isServiceEnabled,
                            onClick = {
                                viewModel.setServiceStats(!state.isServiceEnabled)
                            },
                            role = Role.Switch
                        ),
                    horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.SpaceBetween,
                    verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically,
                    ) {
                    Text(text = stringResource(R.string.notifications_filter))
                    Switch(
                        checked = state.isServiceEnabled,
                        onCheckedChange = { checked ->
                            viewModel.setServiceStats(checked)
                        }
                    )
                }
                Divider()
                Row(
                    modifier = Modifier
                        .fillMaxWidth()
                        .showcase(2, notifyMeMsg1)
                        .showcase(3, notifyMeMsg2)
                        .padding(vertical = spacing.spaceMedium)
                        .selectable(
                            selected = state.isNotifyMeEnabled,
                            onClick = {
                                if (state.isNotifyMeEnabled) {
                                    viewModel.onEvent(NotificationSettingsEvent.CancelNotifyMe)
                                } else {
                                    viewModel.onEvent(NotificationSettingsEvent.ShowNotifyMeTimePicker)
                                }
                            },
                            role = Role.Switch
                        ),
                    horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.SpaceBetween,
                    verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically,
                ) {
                    Column {
                        Text(text = stringResource(R.string.notify_me))
                        Text(
                            text = stringResource(R.string.notify_me_description),
                            textAlign = TextAlign.Start
                        )
                    }
                    Switch(
                        checked = state.isNotifyMeEnabled,
                        onCheckedChange = { checked ->
                            if (!checked) {
                                viewModel.setNotifyMeTime(-1, -1)
                            } else {
                                viewModel.onEvent(NotificationSettingsEvent.ShowNotifyMeTimePicker)
                            }
                        }
                    )
                }
                Divider()
                Row(
                    modifier = Modifier
                        .fillMaxWidth()
                        .padding(vertical = spacing.spaceMedium)
                        .selectable(
                            selected = state.isDeliveryTestingMode,
                            onClick = {
                                viewModel.onEvent(
                                    NotificationSettingsEvent.OnSetDeliveryTestingMode(!state.isDeliveryTestingMode)
                                )
                            },
                            role = Role.Switch
                        ),
                    horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.SpaceBetween,
                    verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically,
                ) {
                    Column(modifier = Modifier.weight(1f)) {
                        Text(text = "Delivery testing mode")
                        Text(
                            text = "Replace hourly delivery boundaries with 3-minute boundaries for faster testing.",
                            style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodySmall,
                            color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant,
                        )
                    }
                    Switch(
                        checked = state.isDeliveryTestingMode,
                        onCheckedChange = { enabled ->
                            viewModel.onEvent(NotificationSettingsEvent.OnSetDeliveryTestingMode(enabled))
                        }
                    )
                }
                TextButton(
                    onClick = { viewModel.onEvent(NotificationSettingsEvent.ClearBudgetSpend) },
                    modifier = Modifier.padding(bottom = spacing.spaceSmall),
                ) {
                    Text(
                        text = "Clear budget spend (debug)",
                        color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.error,
                    )
                }
                val timePickerState = rememberTimePickerState()
                if (state.isTimePickerVisible) {
                    Dialog(onDismissRequest = {
                        viewModel.onEvent(NotificationSettingsEvent.DismissNotifyMeTimePicker)
                    }) {
                        Surface(
                            shape = MaterialTheme.shapes.extraLarge,
                            tonalElevation = AlertDialogDefaults.TonalElevation
                        ) {
                            Column(
                                modifier = Modifier.padding(spacing.spaceLarge)
                            ) {
                                TimePicker(
                                    state = timePickerState,
                                )
                                Row(
                                    modifier = Modifier
                                        .fillMaxWidth(),
                                    horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.End
                                ) {
                                    TextButton(onClick = {
                                        viewModel.onEvent(NotificationSettingsEvent.DismissNotifyMeTimePicker)
                                    }) {
                                        Text(
                                            text = stringResource(id = R.string.cancel),
                                            style = MaterialTheme.typography.labelLarge
                                        )
                                    }
                                    Spacer(modifier = Modifier.width(spacing.spaceSmall))
                                    TextButton(onClick = {
                                        viewModel.onEvent(
                                            NotificationSettingsEvent.SaveNotifyMeTime(
                                                timePickerState.hour,
                                                timePickerState.minute
                                            )
                                        )
                                    }) {
                                        Text(
                                            text = stringResource(id = R.string.ok),
                                            style = MaterialTheme.typography.labelLarge
                                        )
                                    }

                                }
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
                AnimatedVisibility(visible = state.isNotifyMeEnabled) {
                    Column(
                        modifier = Modifier
                            .fillMaxWidth()
                            .padding(vertical = spacing.spaceSmall)
                            .clickable {
                                viewModel.onEvent(NotificationSettingsEvent.ShowNotifyMeTimePicker)
                            },
                    ) {
                        if (state.notifyMeHour != -1) {
                            Text(text = "${state.notifyMeHour}:${state.notifyMeMinute}")
                        }
                        Spacer(modifier = Modifier.height(spacing.spaceExtraSmall))
                        Text(text = stringResource(R.string.tap_to_set_new_time))
                    }
                }
                Divider()
            }

        }
    }

    dialogQueue
        .reversed()
        .forEach { permission ->
            PermissionDialog(
                permissionTextProvider = when (permission) {
                    Manifest.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS -> PostNotificationPermissionTextProvider()
                    Manifest.permission.SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM -> ScheduleExactAlarmPermissionTextProvider()
                    else -> return@forEach
                },
                isPermanentlyDeclined = !shouldShowRational(permission),
                onDismiss = { viewModel.onEvent(NotificationSettingsEvent.DismissPermissionDialog) },
                onOkClick = {
                    viewModel.onEvent(NotificationSettingsEvent.DismissPermissionDialog)
                    if (permission == Manifest.permission.SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM) {
                        viewModel.openExactAlarmsPermissionScreen()
                    } else {
                        postNotificationPermissionResultLauncher.launch(
                            permission
                        )
                    }
                },
                onGoToAppSettingsClick = {
                    if (permission == Manifest.permission.SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM) {
                        viewModel.openExactAlarmsPermissionScreen()
                    } else {
                        viewModel.openAppSettings()
                    }
                    viewModel.onEvent(NotificationSettingsEvent.DismissPermissionDialog)
                }
            )
        }
    if (state.isWarningDialogVisible) {
        MyDialog(onDismissRequest = {}) {
            var doNotShowAgain by rememberSaveable {
                mutableStateOf(false)
            }
            Text(text = stringResource(id = R.string.notification_filter_warning_title), style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleLarge)
            Text(text = stringResource(id = R.string.notification_filter_warning_message))
            Row(
                modifier = Modifier
                    .selectable(
                        selected = doNotShowAgain,
                        onClick = { doNotShowAgain = !doNotShowAgain },
                        role = Role.Checkbox
                    ),
                verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically
            ) {
                Text(text = stringResource(id = R.string.do_not_show_again))
                Checkbox(checked = doNotShowAgain, onCheckedChange = {doNotShowAgain = it})
            }
            Row {
                TextButton(onClick = {
                    viewModel.onEvent(
                        NotificationSettingsEvent.DismissWarningDialog(
                            doNotShowAgain
                        )
                    )
                }) {
                    Text(text = stringResource(id = R.string.i_understand))
                }
                Spacer(modifier = Modifier.width(spacing.spaceMedium))
                TextButton(onClick = {
                    viewModel.onEvent(NotificationSettingsEvent.OnShouldShowcase(true))
                    viewModel.onEvent(NotificationSettingsEvent.DismissWarningDialog(false))
                }) {
                    Text(text = stringResource(id = R.string.tell_me_more))
                }

            }
        }
    }
}
